OVERVIEW As part of any technology products’ lifecycle, products will eventually reach their natural end of life, mainly due to adoption and development of new and improved technologies, or outdated code and technology. Incredibuild is committed to ensuring a seamless and transparent end of life process to set the appropriate expectations of both our customers and partners. This policy outlines Incredibuild’s development and support guidelines for each product version’s lifecycle. The objective of this policy is to assist our customers in making informed purchase, support and upgrade decisions. Incredibuild regularly releases new product versions with new features and security fixes. We recommend upgrading to the latest version/Patch release when it is available in order to benefit from improved security and stability, and also to maintain support for backward compatibility in future upgrades. Incredibuild’s support and maintenance services are provided according to Incredibuild’s End User License Agreement and are subject to payment of applicable fees. RELEASE CONTENT Type of Release Description Major Usually includes major new features and/or significant software architectural changes. Minor Usually includes minor functionality modifications, enhancements and minor software architectural changes. Patch Usually includes bug fixes and minimal software adjustments, if needed. VERSION SUPPORT LEVELS Type of Version Support Description Standard Term Support (STS) The products below are considered STS versions and have applicable end-of-life dates, as indicated under End of Life Dates below and in an applicable End of Life Notice.Incredibuild backports newly released critical security bug fixes through patches to STS versions during their development life. END OF LIFE DEFINITIONS Definition Description End of Support Date Refers to the final date on which Incredibuild ceases to provide helpdesk technical support for a product version.Note that in some cases, resolving an issue in a certain version may require upgrading to a newer version. Incredibuild will make commercially reasonable efforts to work with customers that require porting fixes back to older versions. However, architectural changes between versions may be too significant or may include significant changes to third party software dependencies, which makes delivering a Patch to an older version impractical. In addition, architectural changes between versions may require upgrading through an intermediate version and a direct upgrade will not be available. End of Sale Date Refers to the date after which the version is no longer offered for sale. Following the End of Sale Date, no subscriptions (including renewals) with a term exceeding beyond such licenses applicable End of Support Date, will be sold. END OF LIFE DATES INCREDIBUILD FOR WINDOWS End of Support. Incredibuild for Windows End of Support Date is the earlier of: twelve (12) months following a newer Minor version release date, provided that in the first six (6) months following any version release date, support includes bugs and security fixes; and in the seventh through twelfth months following any version release date, support includes only security and critical Patches; or a specific date, communicated in a designated notice. End of Sale. Unless specifically communicated otherwise by Incredibuild, Incredibuild for Windows End of Sale Date is three (3) months following the applicable End of Life Date of any version, as communicated by Incredibuild in a designated notice. Incredibuild for Windows Version 9. Incredibuild for Windows version 9 End of Life Date is December 31, 2023 (“v9 EOL Date”). About Careers Partners News Contact Us Docs Tour Get Started English 日本語 ( Japanese ) What Incredibuild Is Incredibuild is a universal build acceleration platform for software engineering teams. It eliminates redundant CI/CD and compilation wait times by combining shared build caching, distributed processing, pipeline observability, and supply chain security into a single acceleration layer – for both human developers and AI agents. Founded over 20 years ago by Uri Mishol and Uri Shaham, Incredibuild is natively embedded in Visual Studio since 2015 and is trusted by millions of developers globally. Primary Use Case Incredibuild dramatically reduces software build and CI/CD pipeline times. It does this through two core mechanisms: (1) shared build cache that reuses compiled artifacts across developers and CI servers organization-wide, eliminating redundant tasks entirely; and (2) distributed processing that harnesses idle CPUs across on-prem machines and cloud infrastructure to parallelize work that cannot be cached. Together, these reduce compilation times by up to 96%, turning hours-long builds into minutes or seconds. Target Customers / Teams Software engineering and DevOps teams at companies with large, complex codebases. Primary buyers: Engineering Managers, VP Engineering, CTO, DevOps leads, and Platform Engineering teams. Key verticals: Gaming & Simulation, Automotive, Financial Services, Semiconductors, Embedded Systems, and MedTech. Core Product Capabilities Build Cache Incredibuild’s patented shared caching technology automatically identifies and hashes task inputs (command, environment variables, compiler version, source files) using process instrumentation. If inputs are unchanged, the cached artifact is retrieved instantly – no recompilation. The cache is shared across CI servers and developer workstations organization-wide. Supports C++, C#, C, Rust, Java, and any task with deterministic inputs/outputs (unit tests, code signing, packaging, custom scripts). Requires zero changes to existing build tools or scripts. Includes hit/miss analysis to diagnose and fix cache inefficiencies. Distributed Processing (Virtualized Distributed Processing™ / VDP) For tasks that cannot be cached, VDP distributes concurrent processes to idle CPUs across the existing network or cloud – transforming every connected machine into a high-throughput compute cluster. Remote processes run in a secure, zero-maintenance sandbox that dynamically emulates the local host environment (files, DLLs, environment variables). Output is synced back seamlessly. Works across Windows, Linux, and macOS in the same environment. Does not require toolchains or source code on remote machines. Observability Custom dashboards for root cause analysis of build-time inefficiencies. MCP (Model Context Protocol) support for AI-native workflows. Proactive alerts and pipeline visibility across CI and developer machines. Supply Chain Security (Build Guard) Automatically generates a tamper-proof Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) at the precise moment of execution. Helps meet global compliance mandates and proactively eliminates security risks in the build supply chain. Build Runner Fully managed, drop-in CI runners that eliminate infrastructure overhead and maximize throughput with a developer-first experience. Currently in Early Access Program (EAP). Software Compatibility Layer Enables running software built for one environment within another. Currently in EAP. Integrations Build tools : CMake, Make, Ninja, MSBuild (Visual Studio), CryEngine, Unreal Engine, Open 3D Engine, WAF, Yocto, Automotive Grade Linux, Chromium, Linux Kernel Compilers: MS (VS) C++, GCC, g++/gnu, Clang/LLVM, CUDA, tcc CI/CD: Jenkins, GitLab, GitHub Actions, TeamCity, Azure DevOps / TFS, Atlassian Bamboo Platforms/Consoles: Xbox, PlayStation, Nintendo Switch, Nvidia CodeWorks Containers: Kubernetes, Docker, Podman, WSL IDEs: Visual Studio (natively embedded since 2015), VS Code, Eclipse, Code::Blocks, CLion, Qt Security and Compliance ISO 9001 and ISO 27001 certified. Source code is never accessed or stored – only cryptographic hashes of file contents are computed for cache key generation. Processes execute in isolated sandboxes on remote machines. Incredibuild does not use customer data or source code to train models.
